raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [ ] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

CI or test infrastructure

## Summary

Test-only changes under `test/python/moe_ep/`:

- `test_moe_ep_multinode.py`
  - Add `forward-ep8-world8`, the whole-world EP8 inference-forward case that was missing next to ep4/ep6/ep12/ep16.
  - After every case, shut the MegaMoE runtime down and barrier on the EP group. Destroy the process group only for subgroups, never for `WORLD`.
- `test_moe_ep_backward.py`
  - In the two EP2 training-graph overflow tests (`test_training_graph_error_mode_overflow_asserts_on_all_ep2_ranks`, `test_training_graph_drop_mode_overflow_completes_forward_and_backward`), prepend `test/python` to the probe subprocess's `PYTHONPATH`. Any existing value is kept.

## Why

- **Runtime teardown.** The runtime manager stays alive after `op.close()` and stays bound to the EP group's membership. The test used to shut it down only after subgroup cases. Previously the `WORLD` cases always ran last, so this never mattered. With `forward-ep8-world8` running before `forward-ep6-world8`, the runtime was still bound to the 8-PE `WORLD` group. The ep6 case was then refused with `already bound to a different EP subgroup`, its teardown no longer matched the idle ranks' barrier, and the run hung until the 10-minute NCCL timeout.
- **Probe `PYTHONPATH`.** `probe_moe_ep_training_graph.py` runs under `torch.distributed.run` in a fresh interpreter. Its `sys.path` starts at the probe's own directory (`test/python/moe_ep/`), so `from moe_ep.moe_ep_test_support import ...` only worked if the caller had exported `PYTHONPATH=test/python`. Without that, both tests fail with `No module named 'moe_ep'`. Setting the path in the test makes it independent of how the suite is launched.

## Related issues

None.

## API and compatibility impact

None. Test-only changes; no library code, public API or supported-version changes.

## Testing

Passed on Rubin (sm107): the two-node world-size-8 multinode test (including the new `forward-ep8-world8` case) and the single-node `test/python/moe_ep` tests.

nodes.body:
**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `8164c452476f` against base `d2e433647b66`.

Thank you for your contribution! Reviewed both changed test files and the runtime lifecycle they exercise. The new WORLD case now shuts down the retained runtime before a later subgroup binds it, while preserving WORLD itself. The subprocess path changes make the test helpers discoverable in a fresh interpreter and retain inherited PYTHONPATH entries. I found no approval-blocking issue. Independent validation below covers host lifecycle and import behavior; the reported native SM107 multinode run remains author evidence.

Validation: Built a fresh Python 3.10 extension from the reviewed head. With Torch 2.11, DSL 4.7 and cuDNN 9.27, the existing runtime-manager tests passed: 4 passed, 71 deselected. Collected all 12 relevant L1 cases, including both new EP8 combine-format cases and the two changed overflow subprocess tests. Ran 96 rank/case/format host lifecycle controls using the exact test function and the real RuntimeManager, with fake provider/collective operations. Sequences covered EP4, EP6 and EP8/WORLD in both directions and both combine formats. Each case released the retained runtime, subgroup destruction matched membership, and WORLD was never destroyed. Replacing the cleanup with the old body while retaining the new WORLD case reproduced the real RuntimeManager error on the following EP6 bind: the runtime was still bound to a different EP subgroup. Checked both changed subprocess environments with PYTHONPATH unset, empty and populated. Four fresh-interpreter helper-discovery checks and four real probe import/--help runs passed, including preservation of inherited paths. The previous environment reproduced ModuleNotFoundError for moe_ep. The --help runs validate imports only and exit before distributed execution. The author reports successful two-node world-size-8 runs including the new EP8 case and single-node MoE EP tests on SM107; I did not rerun those native tests. The public style check passes. Added the applicable existing cat-bugfix, mod-infra and orig-nv-eng labels.

Limitations: This worker has no SM107 device. The host controls replace NVSHMEM and collectives, so they do not establish native NCCL/NVSHMEM progress, distributed race freedom or GPU numerical correctness. L1 collection is not execution. I did not start a CI run: the available default Python lane excludes these L1 cases, and the generic multi-GPU smoke target does not exercise this multinode MoE EP suite. Native coverage remains the author's reported run. The merge-metadata check still requires project and milestone assignment. Project access is unavailable with this token's scope, and the PR does not state a release target from which to select a milestone. These metadata limitations are separate from the code review.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
